Here’s what I found out about the announcement and what it actually means. The information comes from SDCCD’s own documents and reporting by local media (NBC 7 San Diego), among other independent summaries.

---

### What Actually Happened

**Official Source**  
- On November 16, 2026, the San Diego Community College District (SDCCD) posted a press release confirming that starting **January 1, 2027**, eligible employees will be entitled to **up to a full year (52 weeks)** of fully paid leave after the birth, adoption, or foster-placement of a child. ([sdccd.edu](https://www.sdccd.edu/departments/communications/newscenter/articles/2026/52-week-maternity-leave.aspx?utm_source=openai))  
- The leave also covers pregnancy-related disabilities, must be taken within the child’s first year of life, and in the case of adoption or foster placement, the child must be under **age five**. ([sdccd.edu](https://www.sdccd.edu/departments/communications/newscenter/articles/2026/52-week-maternity-leave.aspx?utm_source=openai))  
- It includes **full job protection** and continuation of health benefits throughout the leave. **Employees do not have to use their sick or vacation leave** for this paid leave. ([sdccd.edu](https://www.sdccd.edu/departments/communications/newscenter/articles/2026/52-week-maternity-leave.aspx?utm_source=openai))  

**Eligibility and Coverage**  
- Eligible employees must have **at least 12 months of service** with the district. ([sdccd.edu](https://www.sdccd.edu/departments/communications/newscenter/articles/2026/52-week-maternity-leave.aspx?utm_source=openai))  
- The policy covers about **2,217 regular employees** (faculty, classified professionals, supervisors, managers) plus **over 2,000 adjunct faculty**. ([sdccd.edu](https://www.sdccd.edu/departments/communications/newscenter/articles/2026/52-week-maternity-leave.aspx?utm_source=openai))  
- The district estimates the annual cost of the new benefit at **up to $1.2 million**. ([sdccd.edu](https://www.sdccd.edu/departments/communications/newscenter/articles/2026/52-week-maternity-leave.aspx?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Independent Coverage / Media Confirmation

- NBC 7 San Diego reported the same details: the policy takes effect Jan. 1, 2027; applies to both parents and all eligible employees regardless of gender; leave must be used in the child’s first year; adopted or foster children must be under age 5. ([nbcsandiego.com](https://www.nbcsandiego.com/news/local/san-diego-community-college-district-to-offer-year-of-fully-paid-parental-leave/4103585/?utm_source=openai))  
- Noted that this leave is among the most generous in U.S. higher education, given most colleges and universities offer an average of seven weeks of paid parental leave and fewer than 5% offer more than 12 weeks. ([sdccd.edu](https://www.sdccd.edu/departments/communications/newscenter/articles/2026/52-week-maternity-leave.aspx?utm_source=openai))  

---

### What Was Announced vs. What Is Measured / Complete

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Announcement / Plan** | SDCCD has announced and agreed (via labor unions) to institute the fully paid parental leave benefit. The policy is not yet in effect—implementation begins **January 1, 2027**. ([sdccd.edu](https://www.sdccd.edu/departments/communications/newscenter/articles/2026/52-week-maternity-leave.aspx?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Measured / Outcome** | The actual measured outcomes (e.g. how many employees take it, retention impacts, cost vs estimate) are not yet available—as of Nov. 18, 2026. This is because the policy hasn’t begun yet. |

---

If you want, I can try to find if there’s earlier precedent details (other institutions with similar leave), or projections of expected impact once this takes effect.

stories.research_notes:
Here’s a factual research note on the candidate claim “Desflurane Shortens Postoperative Recovery Times Compared to Sevoflurane in Elderly Patients,” based on peer-reviewed studies and clinical trial resources:

---

## What Was the Claim  
That desflurane anesthesia significantly improves (i.e. shortens) recovery time versus sevoflurane in elderly patients after surgery — specifically in terms of “postoperative recovery” outcomes.  

---

## Primary / Original Study Findings

1. **Large RCT from Vienna (RAPID trial; Patients ≥65, minor- to moderate-risk noncardiac surgery, n=190)**  
   - Published in *Journal of Clinical Anesthesia* (2024). ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39121786/?utm_source=openai))  
   - The **primary outcome** was time from arrival to PACU (post-anesthesia care unit) until reaching the discharge readiness criterion of a modified Aldrete score ≥ 12, assessed every 5 minutes. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39121786/?utm_source=openai))  
   - **Result**: No significant difference between desflurane and sevoflurane. Median durations were identical (0 minutes difference) with interquartile range [0;0] for both groups. p = 0.245. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39121786/?utm_source=openai))  
   - Other outcomes (postoperative nausea/vomiting, BIS values, S100-B biomarker) also showed no significant group differences. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39121786/?utm_source=openai))  

2. **Systematic Review & Meta-analysis (October 8, 2026)**  
   - *Perioperative Medicine* reviewed 10 RCTs, totaling 746 elderly patients (>65 years). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13741-026-00696-z?utm_source=openai))  
   - Found significant benefits for desflurane on *early recovery metrics*: time to open eyes, follow commands, extubation, orientation were all shorter in the desflurane group (with mean differences of a few minutes) compared to sevoflurane, all with statistically significant p-values. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13741-026-00696-z?utm_source=openai))  
   - However, **no significant difference** in recovery room discharge time (i.e. when PACU discharge criteria met) (mean difference −3.27 min; 95% CI −6.66 to 0.12; P = 0.06) and no difference in incidence of perioperative neurocognitive disorder or adverse events. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13741-026-00696-z?utm_source=openai))  

3. **Other Relevant Trials**  
   - In elderly orthopedic surgery patients (n=80), a 2025 RCT found desflurane led to shorter times to eye-opening, extubation, following commands, and shorter PACU stay. Patient satisfaction was higher. Cognitive function (MMSE scores) did *not* differ substantially between groups. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41384106/?utm_source=openai))  
   - In older trials (e.g. Heavner et al., 1998) for patients ≥ 65 and anaesthetics lasting ≥ 2 hours, desflurane significantly shortened “early recovery” markers (eye opening, extubation, orientation) but showed **no** difference in intermediate recovery (time to PACU discharge, cognitive test recovery). ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14504150/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Conclusion: What Actually Happened

- **Completed outcome**: Multiple randomized controlled trials and a recent meta-analysis have been conducted. The meta-analysis (2026) is the most comprehensive summary of existing RCTs. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13741-026-00696-z?utm_source=openai))  
- **Measured outcomes**: Early recovery metrics (e.g. time to open eyes, extubate, follow commands, orientation) *are* significantly faster with desflurane compared to sevoflurane in elderly patients. PACU discharge readiness (meeting Aldrete score ≥ 12) *generally did not differ significantly* in larger trials. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39121786/?utm_source=openai))  
- **So the claim is partly supported**: It is accurate that desflurane shortens some postoperative recovery times (especially early recovery milestones) among elderly patients. But the claim that it “significantly improves recovery times” in a broad sense (i.e. including time to discharge from PACU or full postoperative readiness) is **not uniformly supported**; many studies show no advantage on those later outcomes.  

---

If you want exact numbers (means, medians), or trial-by-trial breakdowns by surgery type, I can pull those up.

stories.research_notes:
Here is a research note on the claim “Drones improve heritage conservation in Segovia,” based on live web sources. It records what has actually happened, citing both original or primary sources and independent coverage.

---

**What happened / Measures taken**

1. **Recognition from DJI to the City of Segovia**  
   On 17 November 2026, the Segovia City Council (Ayuntamiento de Segovia) received an official recognition from the international drone‐company DJI for its work in cultural heritage conservation using drones and digital technologies. ([segovia.es](https://segovia.es/index.php/actualidad/noticias/la-empresa-dji-reconoce-al-ayuntamiento-de-segovia-por-su-apuesta-por-la?utm_source=openai))  
   The acknowledgment was given during a formal event in which Segovia presented specific uses of drones in municipal activities and how these integrate with the city’s digital twin (gemelo digital) for better public management and protection of historic monuments. ([segovia.es](https://segovia.es/index.php/actualidad/noticias/la-empresa-dji-reconoce-al-ayuntamiento-de-segovia-por-su-apuesta-por-la?utm_source=openai))

2. **Concrete applications: Acueducto and Alcázar**  
   - Drones are being used to carry out visual inspections of the Acueducto of Segovia, especially in high or hard‐to‐access areas, reducing the need for scaffolding except in places where physical access by technicians is necessary. ([segovia.es](https://segovia.es/index.php/actualidad/noticias/la-empresa-dji-reconoce-al-ayuntamiento-de-segovia-por-su-apuesta-por-la?utm_source=openai))  
   - Similarly, the Alcázar is documented from the air using drone technology to capture data from towers, facades, and roof zones which are otherwise difficult to reach. ([elperiodico.digital](https://www.elperiodico.digital/ciencia/segovia-usa-drones-para-crear-gemelos-digitales-del-patrimonio-533844.html?utm_source=openai))

3. **Digital twin / 3D models**  
   Segovia has a digital twin of its old town (casco histórico), created in partnership with Esri España. It is a 3D model built from aerial photographs that allows users to measure façades, inspect roof coverings, analyze the surroundings of monuments, and access a public viewer to “virtually walk” through the city. ([segovia.es](https://segovia.es/index.php/actualidad/noticias/la-empresa-dji-reconoce-al-ayuntamiento-de-segovia-por-su-apuesta-por-la?utm_source=openai))  
   In addition, monuments such as the Acueducto and the Alcázar now have detailed tridimensional replicas (digital models) made with professional DJI solutions, with high spatial resolution, enabling precise documentation, monitoring, and planning for conservation. ([larazon.es](https://www.larazon.es/tecnologia/esta-ciudad-espanola-utilizado-drones-preservar-herencia-patrimonio-humanidad_202611176afc9586f6b335433bb38653.html?outputType=amp&utm_source=openai))

4. **DJI’s World Heritage 3D Conservation Initiative**  
   DJI hosted an award ceremony in Segovia, in connection with its “World Heritage 3D Conservation Initiative.” At the event, winners of video fly‐throughs (3D reconstructions) of cultural or natural heritage sites globally were presented. Segovia was highlighted as a leading example for using advanced drone tools in heritage conservation and urban planning. ([mynewsdesk.com](https://www.mynewsdesk.com/uk/dji/news/dji-honors-world-heritage-3d-conservation-initiative-winners-at-ceremony-in-segovia-spain-515085?utm_source=openai))

---

**Completed / Measured Outcomes vs Plans or Announcements**

- Completed outcomes include:
  * The city already received an award/recognition from DJI (actual event on 17 November 2026). ([segovia.es](https://segovia.es/index.php/actualidad/noticias/la-empresa-dji-reconoce-al-ayuntamiento-de-segovia-por-su-apuesta-por-la?utm_source=openai))  
  * The creation of 3D models / a digital twin for the Acueducto, Alcázar, and the historic center. These models are already in use for documentation, inspection, and planning. ([larazon.es](https://www.larazon.es/tecnologia/esta-ciudad-espanola-utilizado-drones-preservar-herencia-patrimonio-humanidad_202611176afc9586f6b335433bb38653.html?outputType=amp&utm_source=openai))  
  * Active use of drones to inspect elevated or difficult‐to‐access parts of monuments. ([segovia.es](https://segovia.es/index.php/actualidad/noticias/la-empresa-dji-reconoce-al-ayuntamiento-de-segovia-por-su-apuesta-por-la?utm_source=openai))

- Plans / announcements or future potential include:
  * That these tools will help in detecting damage early, reducing cost/time of inspections. (Part of the justification cited by the city’s officials.) ([segovia.es](https://segovia.es/index.php/actualidad/noticias/la-empresa-dji-reconoce-al-ayuntamiento-de-segovia-por-su-apuesta-por-la?utm_source=openai))  
  * The World Heritage 3D Conservation Initiative is an ongoing DJI program intended to encourage more conservationists worldwide to adopt these methods. ([mynewsdesk.com](https://www.mynewsdesk.com/uk/dji/news/dji-honors-world-heritage-3d-conservation-initiative-winners-at-ceremony-in-segovia-spain-515085?utm_source=openai))

---

**Independent Sources & Credibility**

- The original or primary source is the Segovia municipal site, with the news of the award and description of practices, including quotes from officials. ([segovia.es](https://segovia.es/index.php/actualidad/noticias/la-empresa-dji-reconoce-al-ayuntamiento-de-segovia-por-su-apuesta-por-la?utm_source=openai))  
- Independent reporting includes *La Razón* and *El Periódico Digital*, which cover the use of drones and digital twins for heritage conservation, quoting the same examples (Acueducto, Alcázar) and describing what has been done. ([larazon.es](https://www.larazon.es/tecnologia/esta-ciudad-espanola-utilizado-drones-preservar-herencia-patrimonio-humanidad_202611176afc9586f6b335433bb38653.html?outputType=amp&utm_source=openai))  

---

**Dates / Relevant Timeline**

- Recognition awarded: **17 November 2026**. ([segovia.es](https://segovia.es/index.php/actualidad/noticias/la-empresa-dji-reconoce-al-ayuntamiento-de-segovia-por-su-apuesta-por-la?utm_source=openai))  
- Digital twins / models and drone inspections are already in place as of that date. ([segovia.es](https://segovia.es/index.php/actualidad/noticias/la-empresa-dji-reconoce-al-ayuntamiento-de-segovia-por-su-apuesta-por-la?utm_source=openai))

---

**Conclusions**

- Yes, drones are **being used in Segovia** in concrete, measurable ways for heritage conservation: inspections, digital modeling, documentation.  
- The city has moved beyond just plans or announcements; there are completed models and use of drone inspections, with tools already in application.  
- The recognition by DJI further confirms implementation.  

If you want, I can check the technical specs or precision (e.g. what resolution, sensor types etc.) or the cost / impact figures.
